newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower amid profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower amid profit taking.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Monday in quiet trading amid profit taking, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.68 percent, or 1.80 points, to 264.04 on all-share turnover of 126 million shekels against 115 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.60 percent lower at 271.63.

"The market was quiet today and activity was low. It closed slightly lower on profit taking. I believe that the market is only gaining strength before the Maof will break through the 278 level (its all time high set on February 18)," said Ari Eidelhet at Zeler Eblagon Securities.
"The market still looks very good and the trend is positive. The indices need to stabilise before the market can resume its rise," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.
"The fact that the market is declining on low volume is a positive indicator showing that the trend is positive," Eidelhet added.

The most active shares were Israel Discount Bank, which fell 1.5 percent to 362 agorot on volume of 8.1 million shekels; Discount Investments which lost 2.0 percent to 28,227 agorot on turnover of 5.8 million shekels; and Bank Leumi, which gained 2.0 percent to 541 agorot on volume of 5.3 million shekels.
